title: Exchange Online: cross-tenant message recall, controlled by an allow list
summary: The briefing's receiving-tenant controls, disabled default and licensing context are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The blog's deployment window should be described as its published plan rather than confirmation that deployment started.

claims.claim: Exchange Online supports cross-tenant message recall controlled by an allow list.
claims.quote: With Cross-Tenant Message Recall, a tenant admin can add other Microsoft 365 tenants to an allow list.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is August CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "August CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Android, Desktop, iOS, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap associates this change with Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft 365"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-14T23:03:47.
Before this enhancement, message recall worked only within one tenant.
claims.quote: Until now, all these capabilities shared one boundary: Message Recall only worked within a single tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes recall to other organisations that add the sender's tenant to their recall allow list.
claims.quote: Today, you can recall messages only within your organization. Cross-tenant recall will let you recall messages sent to other organizations that add your tenant to their recall allow list.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The receiving tenant's administrator controls cross-tenant recall.
claims.quote: Control sits with the receiving tenant – the organization whose users received the messages.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A cross-tenant recall is honoured only when the receiving administrator has explicitly allow-listed the sender's tenant.
claims.quote: A cross-tenant recall is only honoured when the receiving tenant’s admin has explicitly allow-listed the sender’s tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Senders in allow-listed tenants can recall messages they sent to recipients in the receiving tenant.
claims.quote: Once a tenant is on the list, senders from those allow-listed tenants can recall messages they’ve sent to recipients in the receiving tenant – just as they would for an intra-tenant recall.

claims.claim: If the sender's tenant is not allow-listed, the recall fails.
claims.quote: If Fabrikam isn't on Contoso’s allow list, the recall fails.

claims.claim: The sender's recall status report says the message cannot be recalled across organisations when the sender's tenant is not allow-listed.
claims.quote: The Fabrikam sender sees in the recall status report that the message can’t be recalled across organizations.

claims.claim: An authorised cross-tenant recall is processed like a standard recall against the receiving mailbox.
claims.quote: Because Contoso allow-listed Fabrikam, the recall is honored and processed like a standard recall against the Contoso recipient’s mailbox.

claims.claim: The cross-tenant settings are configured using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Admins can configure these settings by using Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Cross-tenant recall is disabled by default and requires receiving-administrator opt-in.
claims.quote: First, enable or disable cross-tenant message recall for the receiving tenant. Set this parameter to `$True` to turn on the capability. Set it to `$False` (default) to turn it off:

claims.claim: The Exchange blog says no cross-tenant recall occurs until an administrator adds at least one tenant to the allow list.
claims.quote: The feature is disabled by default; no cross-tenant recall occurs until an admin adds at least one tenant to the allow list.

claims.claim: The Exchange blog was published in July 2026 and updated in September 2026.
claims.quote: Jul 10, 2026 ... Updated Sep 15, 2026

claims.claim: The blog says deployment started in mid-August and was due to complete by mid-September.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant Message Recall will start to deploy to worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet starting mid-August, completing by mid-September.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The blog post targeted deployment to start in mid-August and complete by mid-September 2026."

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Receiving-tenant recipient recall notifications apply to cross-tenant recalls when enabled.
claims.quote: If the receiving tenant has enabled recipient recall notifications, those notifications apply to cross-tenant recalls as well.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The recall agent attempts to hard-delete the original message from recipient mailboxes.
claims.quote: The Message Recall feature agent intercepts these recall messages and attempts to hard-delete the message from recipient mailboxes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Recalled messages in mailboxes with Litigation Hold or In-Place Hold show up in eDiscovery.
claims.quote: For mailboxes that have a Litigation or an In-Place Hold, the recalled message shows up in eDiscovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The allow list contains tenant IDs.
claims.quote: Specify external tenants to add or remove from the allowed list. Add the tenant IDs of the organizations you trust to perform recalls:

claims.claim: Allow-listing governs inbound recalls into the receiving tenant.
claims.quote: Allow-listing governs inbound recalls into the receiving tenant.

claims.claim: Each organisation independently decides which external tenants it trusts to recall its mail.
claims.quote: Each organization decides independently which external tenants it trusts to recall messages from its mailboxes.

claims.claim: A sender in the external tenant initiates each recall.
claims.quote: A sender at Fabrikam recalls a message they previously sent to a recipient at Contoso.

claims.claim: The recall system continues attempting recall for up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: The system continues to recall for up to 24 hours.

claims.claim: Recipient recall notifications are optional.
claims.quote: Optional recall notifications for recipients:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Recalls do not appear in mailbox audit logs at the time described by Learn.
claims.quote: Do recalls show up in the mailbox audit logs? No, not at this time.

claims.claim: Message trace and the sender's recall report can be used to verify recall status.
claims.quote: Recall reports build their information based on message trace data. If you don't receive the recall report or if it doesn't update properly, use message trace to verify the recall status.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Cloud mailboxes cannot recall messages sent to on-premises Exchange mailboxes in hybrid setups.
claims.quote: For hybrid customers, you also can't recall messages sent to the on-premises Exchange environment from cloud mailboxes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Cross-tenant recall operates between two tenants in Exchange Online, not over the internet or outside the Exchange Online boundary.
claims.quote: The new message recall feature works within the confines of an organization or Cross-Tenant (between two tenants in Exchange Online ...). You can't recall messages over the internet, or across organizations outside Exchange Online boundary.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Cross-tenant recall is a capability inside licensed Exchange Online; each user accessing the service must be assigned a subscription plan.
claims.quote: Each user who accesses the Exchange Online service must be assigned to a subscription plan, and each user subscription has its own mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate licence, price or meter specific to cross-tenant recall.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant message recall licensing price meter subscription Exchange Online. Read the recall Learn page, Exchange Online service description and Exchange cross-tenant recall blog; none names a separate cross-tenant recall licence, price or meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The recall page names the Premium Encryption in Office 365 service plan for recalling encrypted messages.
claims.quote: Recalling messages encrypted with OME or MIP labels is supported if a sender is assigned Premium Encryption in Office 365 (PREMIUM_ENCRYPTION) service plan and triggers a recall in Outlook on the Web or new Outlook.

claims.claim: The roadmap record lists no charge and no add-on.
claims.quote: We're enhancing the Exchange Online Message Recall feature to add support for cross-tenant recalls.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -CrossTenantRecallEnabled $true enables cross-tenant recall for the receiving tenant.
claims.quote: Set this parameter to `$True` to turn on the capability. ... Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -CrossTenantRecallEnabled <$true | $false>

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -AllowedSenderTenantIds @{Add="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"} adds sender tenant IDs; the parameter also supports removal.
claims.quote: Specify external tenants to add or remove from the allowed list. ... Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration -AllowedSenderTenantIds @{Add="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"}; {Remove="<tenantId 1>","<tenantId 2>"}

claims.claim: The sending tenant's administrator can supply its tenant ID using Get-ConnectionInformation | fl TenantID.
claims.quote: The administrator of the sending tenant can retrieve the tenant ID by running the following command: Get-ConnectionInformation | fl TenantID

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for the cross-tenant enable switch or sender tenant allow list.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant message recall Exchange admin center UI CrossTenantRecallEnabled AllowedSenderTenantIds. Read recall Learn page and cross-tenant blog; search also returned EAC overview. Cross-tenant configuration is documented in PowerShell, not an admin UI.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The recall Learn page does not name the Exchange role required to run Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-CrossTenantRecallConfiguration permissions role AllowedSenderTenantIds CrossTenantRecallEnabled. Read recall Learn page and cross-tenant blog; they say tenant administrator without naming a management role. Search found no specific role reference.

claims.claim: The blog includes Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in its deployment plan.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant Message Recall will start to deploy to worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet starting mid-August, completing by mid-September.

claims.claim: Recall can be triggered in Classic Outlook, New Outlook, Outlook on the web, Outlook for Mac and Outlook for Android/iOS.
claims.quote: You can trigger Message Recall in the Classic Outlook, New Outlook, Outlook on the web, Outlook for Mac, and Outlook for Android/iOS.

claims.claim: Message recall does not work in Outlook for Windows in Online mode.
claims.quote: Message Recall doesn't work in Outlook for Windows under the following conditions: Outlook is in Online mode.

claims.claim: Message recall does not work in Outlook for Windows when multiple Exchange accounts are configured in the profile.
claims.quote: Message Recall doesn't work in Outlook for Windows under the following conditions: ... Multiple Exchange accounts are configured in the Outlook profile.

claims.claim: Learn describes an existing setting to enable or disable cloud message recall.
claims.quote: Admins can control several settings: Enable or disable the new cloud recall feature.

claims.claim: Learn describes an existing setting governing recall of read messages.
claims.quote: Admins can control several settings: ... Whether to recall messages that were already read.

claims.claim: Learn describes an existing maximum recallable message age setting.
claims.quote: The new Maximum Recallable Message Age setting restricts recalling older messages, with a default setting of 365 days.
